transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Well, I guess what made me come in is... I just keep feeling like I ruined things for everybody lately. Like I'm a total fake in my pipefitting apprenticeship. Which is wild because I actually just finished my associate's degree, and my dad was so proud he bought me this really nice set of wrenches. They're the ratcheting kind, you know? The ones that make getting into tight spots behind boilers way, way easier. We had this huge leak at my aunt's house last Thanksgiving, actually, and it was a whole mess with the turkey getting cold and everything, and I had to crawl under the porch to shut off the main... but anyway, I just feel like I'm letting my family down, and even the younger apprentices at the shop. I get hung up on stuff that I know other people would probably just fix and move on from. I just feel like a complete fraud. Have you ever tried fitting a cast iron pipe? It's super heavy and if you don't line it up right... wait, sorry, what did you ask me? Oh, right, why I'm here. Yeah, just that heavy feeling of letting everyone down over nothing.
Do you often feel nervous or on edge, even when there's no obvious reason to?

Um, nervous? I don't know if I'd call it nervous. I mean, I guess I don't really feel on edge for no reason. Usually if I'm on edge, there's a reason, like when my boss is watching me thread a pipe. Threading machines can be so finicky, especially the older ones. We have this one Rigid machine at the shop that always jams if you don't oil it right, and the oil smells terrible, it gets all over your clothes and you can't wash it out. I tried soaking my work shirts in vinegar once because my mom said it helps with grease, but it just made me smell like a salad dressing for a week. But yeah, no, I don't think I feel nervous out of nowhere. Just, you know, the normal stuff.
Do you often feel sad or empty inside?

Sad or empty? No, I don't think so. I mean, I feel bad about letting people down, but it's not like an empty feeling. Empty is more like... well, like when you drain a hot water heater and it just echoes inside. Have you ever heard that? It's this really hollow sound. We had to drain this massive 80-gallon tank at an apartment complex last week because the heating element completely fried. The maintenance guy there was this older dude who kept telling me how they used to build things to last, which, fair enough, but he wouldn't stop talking while I was trying to hook up the hose. And the hose had this tiny pinhole leak, so it was spraying mist all over my boots. They're Red Wings, so they're waterproof, but still, nobody likes wet socks. Wet socks are the worst, especially when you're working a ten-hour shift. But anyway, what were we talking about? Oh, feeling sad. No, not really sad or empty, just... like I'm a fraud, like I said before.
Do you find yourself having repetitive thoughts that are difficult to stop?

Repetitive thoughts? Um, not really. I don't think I get stuck on thoughts like that. I mean, sometimes I'll get a song stuck in my head, but everybody gets that, right? Like last week, I had that one commercial jingle stuck in my head for three days straight. The one for the local car dealership where the guy yells about slashing prices? It's so annoying. And they play it on the radio constantly at the shop. The guys always leave the radio tuned to this classic rock station, which is fine, but they play the exact same twelve songs every single day. If I have to hear 'Hotel California' one more time while I'm trying to solder a joint, I might actually lose my mind. Soldering is actually really tricky, you have to get the copper pipe just hot enough to draw the solder in, but if you overheat it, the flux burns and it won't seal right. And then you have to cut it all out and start over, which is a massive pain, especially if you're working up on a ladder. I hate working on ladders. My balance isn't great, and I always feel like I'm going to drop my torch. But yeah, no, I don't really have thoughts that I can't stop. Just normal stuff.
Do you find yourself avoiding certain tasks or situations at work because of these feelings of being a fraud?

Avoiding tasks? Well, I guess I've been putting off my isometric sketches lately. It's just... I sit down to draw out the pipe runs and I just feel like I'm doing it all wrong, like someone's gonna look at my blueprints and laugh. So I just don't do them. My instructors at the trade school and my foreman at the shop have been having to chase me down about it. They're like, "Where are those sketches?" and I just make up some excuse. I'm actually really worried I'm going to mess up my apprenticeship over this. I worked so hard to get into this program, you know? It's really competitive. I had to take this huge aptitude test just to get an interview. Math and spatial reasoning and all that. The spatial reasoning part was crazy, they show you these folded up shapes and you have to guess what they look like flat. My dad helped me study for it. He's not a plumber, he's an electrician, but he knows all about that kind of testing. He's been an electrician for like thirty years, mostly commercial stuff. He wired this whole shopping mall once... but yeah, I'm just getting slower at work, too, and I'm terrified I'm going to ruin my chances at getting my certification.
Do you often worry about the future or making mistakes?

Worry about the future? I don't know, maybe a little? But not like, all the time. I mean, I worry about normal things, like whether my truck is going to pass inspection next month. It's an old Ford Ranger, and the suspension has been making this awful squeaking noise every time I go over a speed bump. My buddy Dave—he's a mechanic over at the shop on 4th Street—he said he'd take a look at it for me, but he's been so backed up lately. He works on a lot of fleet vehicles, you know, like delivery vans and stuff, and they always take priority because those companies have contracts. I get it, business is business. But I really need my truck to get to job sites. If I don't have my truck, I can't haul my tools, and then I'm totally useless. It's not like I can take a pipe wrench and a blowtorch on the bus. Could you imagine? The bus driver would probably call the cops. The transit system here is pretty terrible anyway, the buses are always running late, and the routes don't even go out to where the new subdivisions are being built, which is where most of our work is right now. But yeah, making mistakes? I guess I worry about that sometimes, but who doesn't?
Have you been feeling like a fraud at work for a short time or has it been going on for a while?

Well, I guess this whole... depressed stretch, or whatever you want to call it, has been going on for about nine months now. It's just been dragging on. But it really only got super obvious recently when I started messing up at work and avoiding my school stuff. It was easier to hide during the winter, you know? Because in the winter, everyone is kind of miserable anyway. The cold just seeps right into your bones, especially when you're working in an unfinished basement with no heat. You're down there trying to thread a steel pipe, and your fingers are totally numb, even with those thick leather work gloves. I go through a pair of those gloves every couple of months because the threading oil just ruins the leather. It makes them all stiff and gross. You can buy the cheap ones at the hardware store, but they don't protect your hands if you slip with the wrench. My foreman actually got stitches last year because his wrench slipped off a fitting and he slammed his hand right into a concrete wall. It was bleeding everywhere. He didn't even want to go to the hospital, he just wrapped it in a dirty rag and kept working for like an hour before we finally convinced him. Plumbers are stubborn like that. But yeah, about nine months, I'd say.
Have your feelings of being a fraud affected your relationships with friends or family outside of work?

Yeah, I guess it has. Actually, that's kind of what made me come in to see you. I just... I keep feeling like I've ruined things for everybody. Like I'm a total fake in this apprenticeship, and I've let my family down, and even the younger apprentices at the shop. I'm obsessing over stuff that I know other people would probably just fix and move on from, but I can't let it go. Like last week, I was supposed to help my dad with some wiring at his house. He's redoing the whole kitchen, taking it down to the studs. It's a huge project. He bought all these new stainless steel appliances—this massive refrigerator with the French doors and the freezer on the bottom. Those things are so heavy, you need like three guys just to get it up the front steps. Anyway, I was supposed to help him, but I just couldn't face him feeling like such a failure, so I bailed. I told him I had to study. He ended up having to hire one of his old buddies to help him pull the wire through the ceiling. His buddy's name is Frank, he's this huge guy, eats like three sandwiches for lunch every day. Frank used to play minor league baseball back in the eighties, I think. He's got all these crazy stories about riding buses across the country. But yeah, I just feel so guilty about letting everyone down all the time.
How much do these feelings of being a fake affect your overall happiness?

Happiness? I don't know, I guess it affects it. It's hard to feel happy when you're constantly worried someone is going to realize you don't belong there. It's like this heavy weight, you know? Just sitting on my chest. Speaking of heavy weights, we had to move this massive cast-iron boiler out of a basement last Tuesday. Man, those things are ridiculously heavy. It took four of us just to get it onto the hand truck, and even then, we were struggling to get it up the stairs. The stairs in those old Victorian houses are so narrow and steep, it's a nightmare. The homeowner was hovering the whole time, too, which makes it worse. She had these tiny little yappy dogs—Pomeranians, I think? They just kept running around our feet, barking their heads off. I was so terrified I was going to step on one of them while carrying this huge piece of metal. Could you imagine? Dropping a boiler on someone's dog? The liability on that would be insane. My boss has this whole insurance policy for property damage, but I don't think it covers squishing a Pomeranian. He's always complaining about his insurance premiums going up anyway. He says the rates have skyrocketed since that big freeze we had two years ago where half the pipes in the city burst. But yeah, happiness... I'm just not really sure how to answer that.
Do you often feel anxious about being judged or evaluated by others at work?

Anxious about being judged? Um... I don't know if I'd call it anxious, exactly. I mean, I guess I just try to keep my head down and do the work. It's hard to tell what the older guys are thinking anyway. They all have these completely blank expressions, especially when they're inspecting a weld. Speaking of welding, we started learning TIG welding at school last month, and man, it is so much harder than it looks. You have to feed the filler rod in with one hand while controlling the torch with the other, and if your angle is off even a tiny bit, you just melt a giant hole right through the pipe. My instructor, Mr. Henderson, he makes it look like magic. He just glides the torch along and leaves this perfect row of shiny little dimes. He's been welding for like forty years, though. He used to work on the oil pipelines up in Alaska back in the day. He's got all these crazy stories about the moose up there. Apparently, a moose will just walk right up to your truck and lick the salt off the bumper. They're massive, too. Like, way bigger than a horse. If you hit one with your car, the legs just snap and the whole body comes crashing right through the windshield. It's super dangerous. But yeah, judged... I don't really know if I feel anxious about it.
Do you feel like a fake in situations outside of your pipefitting apprenticeship as well?

I mean, yeah, I guess I do. Like I said before, that's kind of the whole reason I came in to see you. I just keep feeling like I've completely ruined things for everybody. It's not just the apprenticeship where I feel like a fake, it's... it's like I've let my whole family down, and even the younger apprentices at the shop who are supposed to be looking up to me. I just get stuck obsessing over stuff that I know anyone else would probably just fix and move on from, but I can't. It just sticks in my head. Speaking of things getting stuck, we had this insane job yesterday where a guy flushed a whole t-shirt down the toilet. Like, a full-sized adult t-shirt. It got completely lodged in the main drain line. We had to use the big power auger to snake it out, and the cable got bound up halfway down. The machine started bucking like a bronco. You have to be so careful with those augers, because if the cable snaps, it can whip around and take your hand right off. My boss knows a guy who lost two fingers that way back in the nineties. He had to get them reattached, but they never worked right again. He said the guy couldn't even hold a wrench properly after that, so he ended up having to get a job at a hardware store just mixing paint all day. I can't imagine doing that, just standing in one spot mixing paint. The fumes in those places always give me a headache anyway. But yeah, feeling like a fake... it's just everywhere, really.
Do you feel like a fake when you're not working or thinking about your apprenticeship?

I think I already said this, but yeah, it's not just at work. It's... it's kind of everywhere. That's honestly what made me come in to see you in the first place. I just keep feeling like I've ruined things for everybody. Like I'm a total fake in the apprenticeship, and I've let my family down, and even the younger apprentices... and it's over stuff I know other people would probably just fix and move on from, you know? But I just get stuck on it. Speaking of getting stuck, I was trying to fix this leaky faucet at my mom's house this weekend. It was one of those old two-handle ones, and the cartridge was completely seized up inside the valve body. I had to use a puller tool to get it out, and even then, I almost stripped the threading. My mom was hovering the whole time, offering me lemonade and asking if I needed help. She means well, but it's so distracting. She always makes this homemade lemonade with fresh mint from her garden. It's actually really good, but she puts way too much sugar in it. I keep telling her she's going to give herself diabetes if she keeps drinking it like that, but she just laughs and says sugar is her only vice. She used to smoke, though, back in the eighties. She quit cold turkey when she got pregnant with my older brother. He's an accountant now, lives out in Denver. He loves it out there because he can go skiing every weekend. I tried skiing once, but I just ended up falling on my butt the whole time. The boots are so uncomfortable, too. They pinch your calves like crazy. But yeah... feeling like a fake... it's just this constant thing, even when I'm not thinking about pipes or tools.
Do you often feel nervous or self-conscious in social situations, like when you're with friends or at family gatherings?

Social situations? Um, I don't know if I'd say I get nervous, exactly. I mean, I guess I just try to blend in and not make a big deal out of things. Family gatherings are usually pretty small anyway, mostly just my mom and a couple of aunts. My Aunt Linda always brings this massive green bean casserole that nobody actually likes, but we all just take a polite scoop so we don't hurt her feelings. She uses those crispy fried onions on top, which are actually the best part, but the beans themselves are always super mushy. She buys them canned instead of fresh, which makes a huge difference. I tried telling her once that blanching fresh green beans is super easy, you just boil them for a couple of minutes and then shock them in ice water so they stay crunchy, but she wouldn't listen. She's really stubborn like that. Kind of like how she refuses to upgrade her flip phone. She still texts by pressing the number keys three times to get a letter. It takes her like ten minutes to send a simple "Happy Birthday" text. It's honestly kind of impressive how fast her thumbs move, though, considering she has arthritis. She takes this turmeric supplement for it that smells awful. It stains her fingers yellow sometimes, too. But yeah, nervous with friends or family... I don't really think I feel self-conscious like that.
Do you feel like you're just pretending to be a competent person in most areas of your life, not just at work?

I feel like we just went over this, didn't we? But yeah, like I keep saying, that's exactly why I made this appointment in the first place. I just constantly feel like I've ruined things for everybody. Like I'm just totally faking my way through the apprenticeship, and I'm letting my family down, and even the younger apprentices... and it's all over stupid stuff that I know anyone else would just fix and move on from. But I can't let it go. 

Speaking of pretending to be competent, though, you should see the drywall guys on the site I was at last week. Total hack job. They were just slapping mud on the seams without even taping them properly first. My journeyman said they're probably getting paid under the table, which makes sense because the general contractor on that job is notoriously cheap. He drives this massive lifted truck that probably costs more than my entire life, but he won't pay for decent materials. Those lifted trucks are so ridiculous anyway. Like, how do you even get your tools out of the bed without a stepladder? I just drive a little hatchback. It's an older Honda, but the seats fold all the way down so I can actually fit a surprising amount of PVC pipe in the back if I angle it right over the passenger headrest. You just have to make sure you don't brake too hard or the pipes slide forward and smack the windshield. I had a buddy who cracked his windshield doing exactly that with a piece of copper pipe. Cost him like three hundred bucks to replace, and the guy who did it left weird black sealant all over the dashboard... but yeah, I just feel like I'm letting everyone down all the time.
Do you feel like you're pretending to be someone you're not when you're with friends or in romantic relationships?

I feel like we're just going in circles here. I mean, I don't know about pretending to be someone else with friends or dating or whatever. It's more just... like I told you, the whole reason I'm even sitting here is because I constantly feel like I've ruined things for everybody. Like I'm just a total fake in my apprenticeship, and I've completely let my family down, and even the younger apprentices... all over mistakes that anyone else would just fix and get over. But I just can't. 

Speaking of dating, though, my last boyfriend was a total disaster. He was an electrician, which you'd think would be cool because we're both in the trades, but he was always acting like his job was so much harder than mine. Like pulling wire is somehow more physically demanding than lugging around cast iron pipe all day. He had this weird obsession with collecting vintage switch plates, too. Like, he'd go to estate sales on the weekends just to look for these old brass light switch covers. He had a whole wall of them in his apartment. It was honestly kind of creepy, like a museum for something nobody cares about. And he never dusted them, so they were always covered in this weird gray film. Dust is actually super gross when you think about it. It's mostly dead skin cells. I read an article once that said mattresses double in weight over ten years just from dust mites and dead skin. That's why I bought one of those hypoallergenic mattress protectors. It's supposed to zip all the way around, but the zipper got stuck halfway when I was putting it on, and I had to use a pair of needle-nose pliers to yank it closed. Pliers are honestly the most versatile tool. I keep a pair in my glovebox just in case. But yeah, I don't know about pretending with friends... it's just this heavy feeling of ruining everything for everyone else.
Do you feel like you're just pretending to be a competent person in your personal relationships, like with friends or romantic partners?

I feel like you're asking me the exact same thing again. Like I've been saying, I don't know if it's about pretending in relationships or whatever. The whole reason I made this appointment is because I just have this overwhelming feeling that I've ruined things for everybody. Like I'm a complete fake at my apprenticeship, and I've totally let my family down, and even the younger apprentices... all over stupid stuff that I know anyone else would just fix and move on from. But I can't. 

Speaking of moving on from things, my sister just got a new dog after her last one passed away. It's a Goldendoodle, which I think is just a fancy way of saying a mutt that costs way too much money. But he is pretty cute, I guess. His name is Barnaby. He has this weird habit of chewing on the baseboards in her hallway. She tried spraying that bitter apple stuff on them, but I swear he actually likes the taste of it. Dogs are so weird like that. My old dog used to eat dirt out of the potted plants on the porch. My mom said it meant he was missing minerals in his diet, so she started buying him this super expensive organic dog food that smelled like seaweed. It came in these heavy bags that I always had to carry up the porch steps for her. I actually threw my back out once lifting one of those bags because I twisted weirdly while trying to open the screen door at the same time. I had to go to a chiropractor who cracked my neck so loud I thought my head was gonna fall off. He had this little skeleton model in his office that was wearing a tiny sombrero. I always wondered where you even buy a sombrero that small. Probably on the internet somewhere. You can buy anything on the internet now. But yeah, the relationships thing... it's just that heavy feeling of ruining everything for everyone.
Do you feel like you're a fake with your friends or family when you're not talking about work?

Are you seriously asking me this again? I don't know how many different ways I can say it. It's not about being a fake with friends or family when I'm not talking about work. The whole reason I'm here is because I just have this constant, crushing feeling that I've ruined things for everybody. Like I'm a complete fraud in my apprenticeship, and I've let my family down, and the younger apprentices... and it's all over things that I know anyone else would just fix and move on from. But I just get stuck on it. 

Speaking of being stuck on things, did I tell you about the glue we use for PVC? That purple primer stuff gets everywhere if you aren't careful. I spilled half a can of it on my work boots last month, and now they have this massive purple stain on the toe. They're Red Wings, too, so they weren't cheap. My dad always told me never to skimp on work boots or mattresses because you're always in one or the other. He used to wear these crazy heavy steel-toe boots when he worked at the plant, and he'd leave them right by the front door so you'd always trip over them when you walked in. We had this really ugly green shag carpet in the entryway back then. I don't know why anyone ever thought shag carpet was a good idea. It's basically just a trap for dirt and Legos. I stepped on a Lego once when I was like eight, and I swear it was the most painful thing I've ever experienced. It was one of those tiny square ones with the sharp corners. I was trying to build a castle, but I couldn't find the drawbridge piece, so I ended up using a piece of cardboard from a cereal box instead. Cereal boxes used to have way better prizes inside. Now it's just like, a QR code you scan with your phone. What kid wants a QR code? Anyway... yeah, I just feel like I'm ruining everything for everyone.
Do you feel like you're a fake or incompetent in areas of your life outside of work, such as hobbies or personal interests?

Okay, are you actually listening to me? Because I feel like a broken record here. It's not about hobbies or personal interests or whatever. I keep telling you, what made me come in is that I just keep feeling like I've ruined things for everybody. Like I'm a total fake in the apprenticeship, and I've let my family and the younger apprentices down over stuff that I know other people would probably just fix and move on from. But I can't. 

Speaking of hobbies, though, I don't even really have time for them anymore. I used to do a lot of bowling when I was in high school. I actually had my own custom bowling ball. It was sparkly purple, kind of like the paint on a bass boat. Bass boats are so incredibly loud, by the way. My uncle has one, and he took me out on the lake last summer, and the outboard motor was so deafening I had a headache for two days. He said it's because it's a two-stroke engine. Two-stroke engines burn oil and gas mixed together, which is why they smell so weird. It smells exactly like the weed whacker my neighbor uses every single Sunday at 7 AM. Who does yard work at 7 AM on a Sunday? It's honestly so disrespectful. I tried using those little foam earplugs so I could sleep in, but they always fall out of my ears during the night. I think my ear canals must be shaped weirdly. I read an article once that said everyone's ear shape is as unique as a fingerprint. Which is crazy to think about. Like, the police could theoretically identify you at a crime scene just by looking at a mold of your ear. I wonder if they actually have a database for that like they do for fingerprints. Probably not, that would take up way too much computer storage. But yeah, I don't know about the hobbies thing... it's really just that awful feeling that I'm ruining everything for everyone.
Do you feel like you're a fake or incompetent in areas of your life outside of work?

I honestly feel like I'm being pranked right now. Are you reading off a script or something? Because I really don't know how many more ways I can explain this to you. It's not about being a fake outside of work. Like I keep saying, the whole reason I came in is that I just keep feeling like I've ruined things for everybody. Like I'm a total fake in the apprenticeship, and I've let my family and the younger apprentices down over stuff that I know other people would probably just fix and move on from. But I can't. 

Speaking of fixing things, my neighbor asked me to look at his garbage disposal yesterday because he knows I'm an apprentice. It was making this horrible grinding noise, like a blender full of rocks. Turns out he dropped a spoon down there. It was one of those really nice, heavy spoons, too, like the kind you get at fancy restaurants. I always wonder if people actually steal silverware from restaurants. I knew a girl in high school who stole a massive wooden pepper grinder from an Olive Garden once. She just shoved it right in her purse. Purses are getting so ridiculously small these days, though. I saw one at the mall last week that was literally the size of a deck of cards. What are you even supposed to put in there? A single stick of gum? Gum actually loses its flavor so fast now anyway. I used to chew that zebra-striped gum when I was a kid, and the flavor would literally last for five seconds. But the temporary tattoos inside the wrapper were pretty cool. I tried to give myself a real stick-and-poke tattoo once with a sewing needle and some pen ink, but it just ended up looking like a weird blue freckle on my ankle. My mom was so mad she threatened to ground me for a month. But anyway... yeah. I just can't shake that awful feeling that I'm ruining everything for everyone.
Has your feeling of being a fake caused problems for you in your relationships or daily life outside of work?

I... I genuinely don't understand why you keep asking about outside of work. Are you even listening to me? No, it is not outside of work. It's the apprenticeship! My instructors and my foreman have had to literally chase me down lately about unfinished sketches and my work being so much slower. 

Speaking of sketches, I actually used to be really into drawing. I wanted to be an animator for Pixar when I was in middle school. The way they animate water now is just insane. I watched this behind-the-scenes thing about how they made the ocean in Finding Nemo, and they actually had to make the water look less realistic because test audiences thought it was real live-action footage. People are so weird about stuff like that. Like back in the day when they first invented movies and people ran screaming out of the theater because a black-and-white train was coming at the screen. I took an Amtrak train to Chicago a couple years ago and we got stuck in the middle of nowhere for four hours because a cow wandered onto the tracks. I don't even know how a cow gets through those heavy chain-link fences. Cows are basically just giant grass puppies, though. I read online that they actually have best friends in their herds, and they get super stressed out if you separate them. Which is kind of sad if you think about it. I wonder how they measure a cow's stress levels. Probably heart rate monitors or something. 

But anyway... no, it's not my relationships or whatever. It's work. I'm just terrified that I'm really close to completely damaging this apprenticeship and the certification I worked so incredibly hard to get.

patient.answer: Sad or empty? No, I don't think so. I mean, I feel bad about letting people down, but it's not like an empty feeling. Empty is more like... well, like when you drain a hot water heater and it just echoes inside. Have you ever heard that? It's this really hollow sound. The maintenance guy there was this older dude who kept telling me how they used to build things to last, which, fair enough, but he wouldn't stop talking while I was trying to hook up the hose. And the hose had this tiny pinhole leak, so it was spraying mist all over my boots. They're Red Wings, so they're waterproof, but still, nobody likes wet socks. Wet socks are the worst, especially when you're working a ten-hour shift. But anyway, what were we talking about? Oh, feeling sad. No, not really sad or empty, just... like I'm a fraud, like I said before.

She just shoved it right in her purse. Purses are getting so ridiculously small these days, though. I saw one at the mall last week that was literally the size of a deck of cards. What are you even supposed to put in there? A single stick of gum? Gum actually loses its flavor so fast now anyway. I used to chew that zebra-striped gum when I was a kid, and the flavor would literally last for five seconds. But the temporary tattoos inside the wrapper were pretty cool. I tried to give myself a real stick-and-poke tattoo once with a sewing needle and some pen ink, but it just ended up looking like a weird blue freckle on my ankle. My mom was so mad she threatened to ground me for a month. But anyway... yeah. I just can't shake that awful feeling that I'm ruining everything for everyone.

doctor.intent: Determine the presence of significant distress or impairment in social or occupational functioning
doctor.question: Has your feeling of being a fake caused problems for you in your relationships or daily life outside of work?

target_item.name: Functional Impairment
target_item.manifestation: My instructors and foreman have had to chase me about unfinished sketches and slower work, and I’m scared I’m close to damaging the apprenticeship and certification I worked hard to get.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking whether the patient's symptoms have caused problems in their relationships or daily life, which directly targets functional impairment.

patient.answer:
I... I genuinely don't understand why you keep asking about outside of work. Are you even listening to me? No, it is not outside of work. It's the apprenticeship! My instructors and my foreman have had to literally chase me down lately about unfinished sketches and my work being so much slower. 

Speaking of sketches, I actually used to be really into drawing. I wanted to be an animator for Pixar when I was in middle school. The way they animate water now is just insane. I watched this behind-the-scenes thing about how they made the ocean in Finding Nemo, and they actually had to make the water look less realistic because test audiences thought it was real live-action footage. People are so weird about stuff like that. Like back in the day when they first invented movies and people ran screaming out of the theater because a black-and-white train was coming at the screen. I took an Amtrak train to Chicago a couple years ago and we got stuck in the middle of nowhere for four hours because a cow wandered onto the tracks. I don't even know how a cow gets through those heavy chain-link fences. Cows are basically just giant grass puppies, though. I read online that they actually have best friends in their herds, and they get super stressed out if you separate them. Which is kind of sad if you think about it. I wonder how they measure a cow's stress levels. Probably heart rate monitors or something. 

But anyway... no, it's not my relationships or whatever. It's work. I'm just terrified that I'm really close to completely damaging this apprenticeship and the certification I worked so incredibly hard to get.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient's symptoms of persistent feelings of being a fake, self-doubt, and fear of being found out, particularly in the context of their apprenticeship, align closely with the diagnostic criteria for a depressive disorder, specifically unspecified depression (F32.9). While the patient does exhibit some anxiety and stress related to their situation, the overarching theme of their feelings of inadequacy and fear of failure points towards a depressive disorder rather than an anxiety disorder (F41.0) or other neurotic disorders (F48.0).
